ex: He's my double cousin as my mother's sister married my father's brother.

ex: a double life

ex: a double bass

ex: When I met the twins, I thought I was seeing double.

ex: The company doubled their earnings per share over last quarter.

senses.d: To increase by 100%, to become twice as large in size.
ex: Our earnings have doubled in the last year.

senses.d: To be the double of; to exceed by twofold; to contain or be worth twice as much as.
ex: Thus re-inforc’d, againſt the adverſe Fleet / Still doubling ours, brave Rupert leads the way.

senses.d: To fold over so as to make two folds.
ex: To make a pleat, double the material at the waist.

senses.d: To clench (a fist).

senses.d: To join or couple.

ex: Laforêt, who (as the French express it), doubles Lainez, that is, performs the same characters in his absence.
[…] and when she attempted to double the part of her mother, she equally failed in playing the great or agreeable lady.
